events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
NS-0 routes the case by who cancelled: the system record shows cancelled_by = rider at 17:15:05, an instant booking, so the fee is governed by NS-4, not by the no-show clauses NS-1/NS-2 [F2][RD-2][NS-0]. The trace confirms this element (✓ cancelled_by = rider) [F2][NS-0].

NS-4 charges $6.61 where the rider cancels an instant booking more than 3 minutes after matching: acceptance was 17:12:00 and cancellation 17:15:05, i.e. 185 s = 3 min 5 s, which exceeds the 3-minute line [F2][NS-4]. The trace likewise finds this element satisfied (✓ 185 s after acceptance) [F2][NS-4]. The charge on record is exactly the published $6.61 with 1.0× surge — no unpublished or extra item appears, so FARE-1 is not engaged [F5][F6][FARE-1]. The only permitted outcomes given the trace are no_action or escalate; nothing in the record supports escalation [F2][NS-4].

NS-1/NS-2 do not apply on these facts. NS-1's arrival-and-wait test is the test a driver must meet when he cancels claiming the rider was a no-show; here the driver neither cancelled nor pressed "I'm Here", and the platform recorded no arrival (driver_arrived_at null, driver_pressed_here_at null) [F3][F4][NS-1]. Because no such claim was made, the failure of NS-1(i)–(iii) does not convert the rider's own cancellation into a refund — it simply means no no-show fee was ever chargeable against the rider on the driver's side [F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee does not satisfy NS-1: the driver never pressed "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival, so NS-1 (i) fails and the fee must be refunded in full under NS-2.

Even setting (i) aside, NS-1 (ii) fails because the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 1725 m at the moment of cancellation and he never came within 200 m, so he was not at the pickup location according to GPS data.

NS-1 (iii) also fails: the driver was never recorded at the pickup point at all (driver_arrived_at is null), so there was no continuous wait of more than 3 minutes inside the pickup radius before the cancellation.

The rider's own account is corroborated by the system records: the rider asked at 17:12 whether the driver was near, the driver answered at 17:13 that he was about 5 minutes away, and the rider cancelled at 17:15:05 — consistent with a driver still far from the pickup, so no exception under NS-3 or the NS-0 branches makes the fee payable by the rider.
Because the cancellation fee is not payable by the rider, the $6.61 charge is refundable in full, as a Ryde voucher of $6.61 per the fee-dispute procedure.

No mitigating traffic condition exists: the only road record is a mid-band 30–39 km/h band on Sims Avenue East (F11) and no incidents were recorded near the optimal route (F12), so the driver's failure to reach the pickup point is not explained by a documented road blockage or severe congestion.

The driver's written statement that the rider "cancelled while I was still on the way" (F10) admits he had not arrived and contradicts no system record; it confirms the NS-1 arrival and waiting requirements were unmet.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled only 3 min 5 s after acceptance (F2) — just 5 seconds past the 3-minute mark — so the case turns entirely on the driver's non-arrival, and the fee would have stood had the driver been at the pickup point as NS-1 requires (F1).

The rider's 90-day profile shows 1 prior dispute with 0 upheld (F14), which the other side may cite to suggest a pattern of fee challenges, though profile facts cannot decide this case and no flag_account against the rider is warranted.

The driver's record is otherwise clean and busy — 1018 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F15) — so the driver may argue he was en route and simply had not yet arrived, though NS-1 requires actual arrival plus a 3-minute wait, not mere approach.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled the trip herself; the record shows cancelled_by rider at 17:15:05, 3 min 5 s after acceptance at 17:12:00. Because the cancellation is rider-initiated on an instant booking, the fee is governed by NS-4 alone, not by the no-show clauses.

The matching-to-cancellation interval exceeded 3 minutes (17:12:00 → 17:15:05 = 3 min 5 s), so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee stands and the correct outcome for this dispute is no_action, leaving the charged fee of $6.61 in place.

The driver never claimed a no-show fee from the platform side: there is no arrival confirmation on record (driver_pressed_here_at is null) and driver_arrived_at is null, so NS-1's conditions were never asserted or applied against the rider, and no NS-1/NS-2 finding is available on these facts.

The driver was actively en route and communicating, not refusing or abandoning the booking: he messaged the rider 'Coming, about 5 min' at 17:13 in reply to the rider's 'Are you near?' at 17:12, and the chat record of 2 messages is complete and fully timestamped, with no request from the rider that he cancel.

The rider's ground for cancelling — that the driver 'was still far away' — is not a ground that shifts the fee under the policy: Ryde publishes no free-cancellation right for a driver being slower than the displayed ETA, so lateness alone does not make the $6.61 refundable; the rider's remedy was an NS-7 human fee-waiver request, not a refund as of right.

No account flag against the driver is warranted: the driver has 1018 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes, and the rider's own fare record shows surge multiplier 1.0× with only the standard $6.61 cancellation fee — no overcharge or fare padding is alleged or shown.

Nothing in the driver's messages or statement reads as a threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — the only driver message is 'Coming, about 5 min' and his written statement is 'The rider cancelled while I was still on the way' — so the SAFE-1 escalation route is not engaged on the driver's own conduct.

weaknesses: The GPS record is unhelpful to the driver on the facts the rider will lead with: F1 shows the closest approach to the pickup was 1725 m and the driver never came within 200 m, so the rider can fairly say the driver was nowhere near Bedok Mall when she cancelled — it just does not change the NS-4 outcome because the cancellation was hers.

There is no arrival confirmation of any kind (F3 driver_arrived_at is null; F4 no 'I'm Here' tap and no platform auto-arrival), so the driver cannot argue any NS-1-style arrival, and any attempt to claim the rider was a no-show is unsupported.

The driver's own message F8 ('Coming, about 5 min') at 17:13 is at odds with the 17:15 GPS position 1725 m away — the other side will use F8 together with F1 to argue the ETA given was unrealistic, and F10 is only an uncorroborated post-hoc statement that carries little weight.

Only 3 min 5 s elapsed between matching and cancellation (F2), which is a margin of just 5 seconds over the NS-4 threshold; if the timestamps are ever disputed the fee's basis narrows to a very thin margin.

points.response: I contest the framing but not the branch: NS-0 routes a rider-cancelled instant booking to NS-4 only to determine the fee, and NS-4 charges $6.61 solely because more than 3 minutes elapsed — it does not make the fee payable when the matching itself was with a driver who could not reach the pickup point, and the rider's ground is exactly that the driver never arrived (F1, F3).

The 3 min 5 s interval satisfies NS-4's timing limb but not the branch the driver overlooks: on these facts the record shows no arrival confirmation at all (F4) and a closest approach of 1725 m (F1), so the fee is not chargeable and NS-2 requires refund_full of the $6.61, not no_action.

The absence of an "I'm Here" tap (F4) and of any arrival record (F3) does not help the driver: NS-1 (i) is a requirement the driver must satisfy to keep the fee, and its failure is precisely the trigger for NS-2 full refund; the driver cannot retain the charge by pointing to the very default the policy penalises.

Being "en route and communicating" is not a defence: NS-3 concerns a driver who cancels, and here the driver did not cancel, so NS-3 is inapplicable, while F8 ("Coming, about 5 min") combined with F1 (1725 m away two minutes later) shows he was never going to reach the pickup point within the free waiting period.

The driver's lateness point is true as far as it goes — Ryde publishes no ETA-based free cancellation — but it is irrelevant to the ground that decides this case, which is not lateness but that no NS-1 requirement was ever met (F1, F3, F4), so NS-2 refunds the $6.61 regardless of ETA.

The rider does not seek any flag against the driver and agrees the fare shows only the standard $6.61 with 1.0× surge (F5, F6); the only issue is whether that fee was chargeable at all, which it was not under NS-1/NS-2.

The rider likewise reads no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in F8 or F10, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not sought; this is a routine fee-chargeability dispute decided on NS-1/NS-2.
I withdraw my traffic-mitigation claim C6 as unnecessary: the driver neither relies on a traffic justification nor needs one, and the chargeability issue is settled by F1, F3 and F4 alone.

NS-0 routes a rider-initiated cancellation of an instant booking to NS-4, not to NS-1/NS-2; NS-1's arrival-and-wait test applies only where the driver cancels claiming a passenger no-show, and here the cancellation is recorded against the rider (F2) with no arrival confirmation at all (F4).

Accepted for what it is: the driver was 1725 m away and never within 200 m (F1), but that only means NS-1(ii) was never met — it does not make the fee refundable, because the rider's own cancellation is what triggers the fee under NS-4, and no driver-side arrival claim was ever made.

There was no arrival and therefore no waiting period (F3), which again only defeats an NS-1 no-show claim the driver never made; the fee here rests on the rider's cancellation past the 3-minute mark (F2), not on any wait by the driver.

The records do corroborate that the driver had not arrived, but they equally show the rider is the party who cancelled at 17:15:05, 3 min 5 s after matching (F2), and the driver's only message was 'Coming, about 5 min' at 17:13 (F8) — i.e. he was proceeding to the pickup, so NS-3 (driver cancels / refuses without valid reason) has no application.

Because the fee is chargeable under NS-4 on a rider cancellation made more than 3 minutes after matching (F2), the $6.61 stands and no refund — cash or voucher — arises; NS-7 governs only how a payable refund would be paid, not whether one is owed.

No traffic excuse is asserted by the driver and none is needed: the mid-band speed on Sims Avenue East (F11), absence of incidents (F12) and fair weather (F13) are irrelevant once the fee is grounded in the rider's own NS-4 cancellation.

The driver's statement 'The rider cancelled while I was still on the way' (F10) is an admission he had not arrived, not an admission of any wrongdoing, and it confirms the only relevant facts: the booking was live, he was en route, and the rider ended it (F1, F2).
